68  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

primary classes, five teachers of commercial students, and twelve teachers of art and music. Although the commercial subjects were not included in a course leading to a college diploma, the College issued a special certificate of proficiency or degree. The music and art were important features of the institution.

Mr. Lewis J. Reynolds, a Senior student in the B.S. course, was one of the faculty 1886-1887 as Professor of Business Penmanship.

The primary teacher listed in College advertising of 1884-1885 were Miss Maggie Toms, who was listed for 1885. Next was Miss Kate Hendershot, who was listed for the school year 1885-1886 in the advertising from Savoy, the College's own training, came to the faculty as Professor of English and Literature. As a student in the College Miss Fannie Jackson taught in a College studio. It is recalled that she was a music teacher. Miss Fannie Chenoweth taught during the year 1880-1890, and Mrs. H. H. Halbell taught for the year of that year. Mrs. Chenoweth (now Mrs. S. P. Smith) and Mrs. Pritchett (now Mrs. Thomas E. Murphy) are both good musicians of the Savoy community. Next, in order named, were Miss Tessie Duebarage, Miss Emma Lucy, M. E. Luther and Miss Lottie Pritchett. Next was Miss Halsell, all of whom had received their training in the College. Miss Halsell, about 1887-1888, was the primary teacher for the last year, and probably the last two years, of the College.

The commercial subjects teachers who instituted the department, there is by the Catalog, are not to be found in the records of the school. Four teachers of Business were Mrs. Jod and Miss Lottie Daniels, about four or five months each semester. Of the list of teachers last named, two were Misses, and in 1888-1890, Miss Jennie Mitchell and Miss Lottie Daniel from the town of Bonham, were among the last.
